name: Liver detox for yellow sclera

lead: Some appearance-focused discussions hold that yellowish eye whites reflect a congested liver and can be cleared with a liver detox or cleanse. The practice is a belief about appearance rather than an established medical treatment.
Medical references describe yellowing of the white of the eye as scleral (conjunctival) icterus, a sign of raised bilirubin, which has liver, blood and bile duct causes.

paras: Proponents link liver function to eye colour. In medical descriptions, bilirubin deposits in the conjunctiva, which binds it readily, and visible yellowing generally indicates serum bilirubin of about 3 mg/dL or more.

Because yellow eyes with yellow skin can accompany hepatitis, cirrhosis, haemolysis or bile duct obstruction, medical sources say it warrants evaluation. Detox products themselves have not been studied for this purpose.

lead: Liver detox for yellow sclera is a belief that yellowish or dull eye whites indicate a burdened liver and can be whitened by cleansing diets, herbs or supplements. No published study has tested a detox regimen for eye whiteness.

Medical sources describe yellowing of the white of the eye as scleral icterus, though the pigment actually deposits in the conjunctiva, which has a high affinity for bilirubin, so it can appear before skin yellowing; visible conjunctival icterus generally indicates serum bilirubin of at least about 3 mg/dL [1]. Causes are classed as prehepatic (excess red cell breakdown), hepatic (liver damage or inherited conjugation defects) and posthepatic (bile duct blockage) [1].

paras: Jaundice from high bilirubin usually involves the conjunctivae and diffuse yellowing of the skin. Carotenemia from large intakes of carotene-rich foods typically spares the conjunctivae and shows mainly on the palms and soles, and some drugs such as rifampin can yellow the skin without jaundice [1]. Gilbert syndrome, found in about 5% of people, involves a less efficient bilirubin-processing enzyme with otherwise normal liver function and usually mild, stress-related jaundice [1]. Medical references note that yellowing with yellow skin should be evaluated because it can signal liver, blood or bile duct disease [1].
